1.answer: When adding an item, the filter computes its k hash positions and sets those bits to 1. When looking up an item, it computes the same k positions and checks those bits; if any bit is 0, the answer is "no"; if all are 1, the answer is "probably yes".
1.quote: Add an item: compute its k positions and set those bits to 1. Query an item: compute its k positions and look at those bits. If any bit is 0, answer "no". If all are 1, answer "probably yes".

2.answer: It can give false positives (saying "yes" for items never added) but can never give false negatives (saying "no" for items that were added). This is because adding items only changes bits from 0 to 1; nothing changes them back to 0.
2.quote: Adding an item only changes bits from 0 to 1. Nothing changes a bit back to 0. So every item you added still has all its bits set, and it always gets "probably yes".

3.answer: You cannot delete an item by clearing its bits because multiple items share the same bits. If you clear a bit for one deleted item, you may clear a bit that another existing item still needs, causing that item to incorrectly answer "no".
3.quote: Dog also uses bit 6. Now a query for dog finds bit 6 at 0 and answers "no", which is wrong. For this reason, a plain Bloom filter does not support deletion.

4.answer: It answers "probably yes", because every item would find all its bits set to 1, regardless of whether it was actually added.
4.quote: As you add more items, more bits become 1, and an unseen item is more likely to find all its bits already on.
